trial_court: Family Court, Dwarka, New Delhi, HMA No. 516/2011 and M No. 132/12
case_name: Smt. Joginder Kaur (Gogi) vs Shri Prit Pal Singh
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Parties were married in 2008; respondent-husband filed divorce petition under Section 13(1)(ia)&(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 on grounds of cruelty and desertion.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging desertion to prove that the other spouse has deserted them for a continuous period of not less than two years.
legal_principles.held: After the amendment, the ground for desertion for claiming divorce under Section 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 requires that one of the spouse who has been deserted by the other for a continuous period of two years immediately preceding the date of the presentation of the divorce petition is entitled to a decree of divorce.

legal_principles.principle: Desertion means the willful abandonment of one's duty or obligations, including living with one's spouse.
legal_principles.held: In general parlance, as per Oxford English Dictionary Vol-1 desertion means 'The action of deserting, forsaking, or abandoning. Willful abandonment of one's duty or obligations, (b) to live with one's spouse.'

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed. The judgment and divorce decree dated 26th February, 2014 in HMA No. 516/2011 are set aside.
